notes.title: War Hospital, out now, is a tug-of-war between empathy and efficiency
notes.notes:
War Hospital, out now on Steam, is about subsisting on the periphery of a war and keeping it firmly off-screen by means of adept time management. Set in 1918, it puts you in charge of a field hospital in northern France, a few minutes drive from the frontline. Here’s how all that works: casualties arrive from the trenches by ambulance or stretcher, and are carried by your medics to a clearing station, where nurses look after them before they’re seen by a doctor. Patients may be lightly or severely injured, but they will all eventually die if they’re left unattended.

notes.title: War Hospital Out Now
notes.notes:
Hello Major,

It's time to join the frontline and take up duty in your military hospital. After 3 years in development, War Hospital is finally available. 

In War Hospital, you play the role of Major Henry Wells, a retired British war doctor requisitioned to take command of a field hospital in the midst of the nightmare of the First World War. Short of staff and supplies, the hospital is the last hope for the many soldiers on the French front.

[previewyoutube=wfYsubi8wGM;full][/previewyoutube]

Your main objectives will be to keep your team's morale up and strengthen the front line with the soldiers you've treated. To do this, you'll need to manage your hospital to accommodate the many wounded who arrive after each battle. You'll need to sort patients by priority before treating them, planning surgical operations or abandoning them to their fate...

Are you ready to make though choices and save lives?

The War Hospital Team

notes.title: Diversity in War Hospital.
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/b897ae34fa888e0cebcbd0edab8fab777037d45d.png[/img]

[h2]How did we achieve diversity? Why does War Hospital only speaks English?[/h2]

In War Hospital, the player manages a British field hospital during World War I on the French front. In order to be able to show the diversity of people fighting and saving lives on the British side of the conflict, we decided on a rather special approach that resulted in War Hospital being available only in the English spoken language version. We invite you to read this story!

When we started building characters who would be the player's advisors in War Hospital, the first thing we did was quite obvious, which was to divide these characters by their specialties. Therefore, we decided that these characters would be:  The head of the nurses' service, the chief engineer, the hospital defense commander, and the leader of reconnaissance units. This is quite an obvious division, characteristic for tycoon like games, which allows players to understand the rules and mechanics of the game. However, when we made this choice, we wanted it to (apart from the game mechanics) also build immersion with the authenticity of the world presented in the game. Our goal was to show the diversity of people who fought on the side of the United Kingdom. Therefore, like Winston Churchill, we used the English language to fight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/8bb3d25a894b1fc0d0917a42939dc91607f36564.jpg[/img]

We decided that our heroes would represent various nations that were part of the British Empire at that time. And with this key we assumed that the chief of engineers was Indian and the messengers were Australians (here, the single-player campaign in Battlefield 1 "The Runner" was a huge inspiration) and the commander of the hospital defense was a Scot. With this decision, we began work aimed at ensuring that for the player these characters do not differ only in their portrait or name. That's why we decided to record the voices of these characters, each of whom speaks differently due to the accent and way of pronunciation typical of their region of the world. We achieved an effect that exceeded our expectations - the characters speak to the player in English, but at the same time he can feel the difference in the way they speak.

This nuance would be extremely difficult to reproduce in other languages, so after many discussions we decided to leave this immersion-building element, limiting the number of spoken languages only to the diversified English language. We hope that this aproach will be appreciated by players.

The War Hospital Team

notes.title: How to show complicate numbers in simple ways - Video Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
Greetings Major,

With only a few days remaining before War Hospital launches, Brave Lamb Studio's devs give you an inside look at the game's economy. 

The human resources and regular resources sectors are the two main economic divisions of War Hospital. All of the medications and semi-finished goods are found in normal resources. Semi-finished items are helpful for building and maintaining your hospital, while medications are helpful for treating soldiers, as you might anticipate. You can order regular ressources, but you'll quickly discover that you'll never have enough, so you'll need to find another way to get them.

Human resources includes surgeons, nurses and medics, nevertheless, as with other resources, the quantity of patients you must cure may quickly overwhelm you, therefore you'll need to manage your staff... and be forced to recruit.

[previewyoutube=Efpmnpp0i1E;full][/previewyoutube]
Don't hesitate to give us your feedback, follow us on Twitter and Facebook and wishlist the game!

Thanks Major,

notes.title: War Hospital has gone GOLD!
notes.notes:
Greetings to the War Hospital community!

We are thrilled to share some monumental news - [b]War Hospital has officially gone Gold[/b]! 🏆

We are delighted to announce that the development phase of War Hospital has been completed after months and years of dedication and hard work. We couldn't be more grateful for your unwavering support throughout, and this marks a significant milestone in our journey.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/82b1ee34f624f9b719f98dbb1d8c85a9467f9ce2.png[/img]

[h3]What is "Going Gold"?[/h3]

In the world of game development, reaching gold status means that the game is ready to be manufactured and distributed. It's a momentous occasion for the entire War Hospital team, as it culminates countless hours of creativity, collaboration and tweaking to create an experience we're truly proud of.

[h3]What is War Hospital?[/h3]

Overcome the challenges of a war hospital by strategically allocating resources, recruiting the best medical staff, and adapting to the ever-changing demands of a war-torn environment. 
Your decisions have an impact on the survival and recovery of patients, so every choice is crucial. Immerse yourself in the intense yet rewarding experience of running a frontline medical facility.

The War Hospital Team 🚑

notes.title: Management is key
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

Management is an important part of a simulation game. In War Hospital, you have to manage your staff:
[list]
[*] Recruiting your staff, so as not to be overwhelmed by the influx of new patients
[*] Managing your staff's working hours, so that you don't end up fainting from overwork.

Dear players, 
 
You have been following our news for a long time and you know that we are committed to making a truly unique game. As the aim of the game is to save people rather than kill them, War Hospital offers a different perspective from other war strategy games. We want to make the game as deep and realistic as possible while respecting the subject it deals with. This is why War Hospital features a range of game mechanics, including management, strategy and role play. notes.title: Dev Diary #4: Hard, Moral decisions as Core Mechanics of War Hospital
notes.notes:
Greetings Major,

War Hospital is not your typical military strategy game. While supporting war effort is present in the game, its focus lies somewhere else. In each soldier’s life. As a major Henry Wells, revered and experienced military medic your role is to do everything possible to save as many soldiers and civilians as possible. But then again, it is not possible to save everybody.

You will have to carefully manage scarce resources and overworked medical staff, facing constant difficult moral choices to do as much as possible. Each patient comes with their own story and in different condition requiring different treatment. It’s up to the player to meet both gameplay challenges and morally difficult choices.


[h2]World War I in the eyes of Hospital Crew[/h2]
Hospital Crew consists of doctors, nurses, medics and engineers. They all have a unique role to fulfill in the medical cycle. Out of all of them, doctors are most involved in patient treatment. Each operation consumes their energy, time and takes a toll on their mental health. Dealing in constant uncertainty of patient wellbeing is not a mere accomplishment.

And in this cycle there is winners. Rehabilitated soldiers go back to the front to face a new danger of death and physical or psychological harm. Each success of saving life is only temporary in the grand scheme of things, that’s why medical effort is so difficult to endure for Hospital Crew. But despite the uncertainty and inevitable doom of the future, one can only do what’s best in their effort to bring temporary respite to those in need.

Because medical assistance is not just about statistical results. It’s about bringing a light of hope to those in need, and sometimes this is what matters the most. In War Hospital player will micro manage their crew and one of our goals was to display that hardship throughout meaningful narrative elements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/6b55d4ca1cf69c8ca3a67e2534ab3e88318901c1.jpg[/img]


[h2]Medical Equipment and healing methodologies in War Hospital[/h2]
World War 1 was a breaking time when it came to innovative ways of harming enemy soldiers. Deadlier machine guns, artillery and even chemical weapons. There were no boundaries in sinister effort during that time. Because of that medical discipline had to catch up rapidly.

During that time medics had to come up with a variety of effective, yet cost efficient methods of treatment. Throughout playing War Hospital, you will have to smartly put into use a broad range of medical devices and methods of operating patients for best possible outcome.

Each of them brings different modifications, not always positive and introduces a variety of possible complications. Risk management and tough calls are present in each patient operation.


[h2]Why British Hospital? How we approach to nations diversity in War Hospital[/h2]
War is a hellish phenomenon. It brings destruction and suffering upon all people involved. The reason why we decided to set up a War Hospital in Britain is due to the fact that British allied forces had the highest diversity of soldiers among them.

Our goal was to show that war tragedy is common for every human, regardless of their nation, age or their history. No matter where does one originate from, the suffering is universal. And that hardship is universal for everybody and in some way it brings people together. They face terrible horrors together and that brings them together. Small acts of kindness, honorable actions, unity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/a9acd3273b565eb5965679e08ab179fb40cfb8c5.jpg[/img]


[h2]Interface as key part of narration[/h2]
While the game revolves around the tragedy of wounded soldiers, player faces gameplay challenges on both micro and macro levels of managing the whole hospital complex. Managing patient operations, assigning best doctor in a given situation and proper tools while under constant scarcity of resources is the core of War Hospital experience.

In order to make all elements as clear and accessible to the user as possible we emphasize iconography, color coding and best design practices to offer a smooth experience for all of you. 


[h2]Ordinary day in War Hospital[/h2]
No day in War Hospital is ordinary. Each day brings new challenges and obstacles to overcome. Constant warfare at front lines, incoming ambulances of wounded soldiers, hunger among citizens and never ending threat of death are present in every moment of gameplay. Player will have to manage all the different systems to keep things going to succeed, to the best of their ability in these harsh conditions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/d166e72993b7fa74766862023155d2c721f6c91e.png[/img]


[hr][/hr]
Finally, we are pleased to share that development of the game is moving forward & well, we shall give you a glimpse of War Hospital gameplay during at [b]Nacon Connect[/b] (the conference of our Publisher) on July 7 at 7:00pm CEST, be sure to follow them on their [url=https://www.youtube.com/c/Nacon]YouTube channel[/url] to be notified once the conference starts!

notes.title: NACON is publishing War Hospital!
notes.notes:
NACON and Brave Lamb Studio are pleased to announce that they have joined forces for the publication of the game War Hospital, a unique strategy and survival game in which the player controls the fate of a British field hospital during the Great War.

In War Hospital players are confronted by the human drama resulting from the terrible conflict that has
so deeply marked our recent history. Every day, when barbarity is unleashed, the hospital doctors have
to deal with the moral dilemmas associated with the dual nature of their task, which is both
humanitarian and military. They fight not only for life but also to maintain their morale and humanity in
a world that seems to have rejected them completely.

In the very creative strategy and survival game segment, War Hospital provides a unique experience
that blends real-time strategy, survival, and RPG elements, while developing a theme rarely dealt with
until now. The game is set in 1917. You play as Major Henry Wells, a British doctor sent to the front to
treat the wounded in an attempt to give a glimmer of hope to the troops. Despite the difficult conditions and the lack of equipment and resources, you must manage how emergencies are handled and develop your hospital.

Thanks to the exceptional support that the British Imperial War Museums gave the developers, the
game faithfully recreates the context of the front and its trenches, as well as the medical equipment
available at the time.

In addition to the deep management gameplay, the game also requires players to make moral choices
that affect the soldiers, the situation at the front, and the battles. The player, therefore, undergoes an
emotional trial through the drama experienced by the soldiers sent into the carnage. The game
broaches the subject of war very differently than is usually the case.

[i]"We are excited to partner with Nacon. We believe that this will help to introduce War Hospital to more
players around the world and show them a different face of war in video games." [/i]stated Michał
Dziwniel, Head of Studio.

[i]“Nacon is especially proud and honored to have been selected by Brave Lambs to work together on the success of War Hospital, a unique game in the genre, once again demonstrating, on the heels of titles
such as This War of Mine and Soldats Inconnus that our media can deal with subjects that are complex
and serious while keeping their identity,” [/i]stated Benoît Clerc, Publishing Director at NACON.

notes.title: War Hospital Dev Diary#3: Sound of World War I field hospital
notes.notes:
Hey there! It’s Marcin, audio lead for War Hospital. Today I’m gonna share with you some inside facts about finding the right sound palette for our game, what approaches we’ve taken and what challenges we’ve encountered along the way! I hope you’ll enjoy it! Let’s dive right into it.

When start working on a project, I usually try to understand the core gameplay alongside the overall mood of the game. After all – game audio is all about feelings and communicating gameplay information. At least that’s my theory :).

The first thing that struck me while doing my research was the fact that there are not so many portraits of WWI in films or games. Couldn’t find any interesting audio tropes and motifs to follow, had to find my own, had to dig deeper! It’s the opposite of what we have available for example for the WWII period. 

In that process, I realized that WWI was a very interesting time – technology and science wise. The latest advancements in communication, like radio and phones, were used on the frontlines to coordinate the troops. It also seems that WWI moved the watches from our pockets onto our wrists for good. What a bizarre fact! I love such things that are so obvious, that you don’t even realize that someone had to come up with them.

I decided to combine my findings into a technological sound palette that I could use as iconic elements of the period. After adding that to our gameplay – which is all about making quick and tough moral decisions while managing a field hospital – I had my essence of audio sauce for that game. 

I want the players to feel that their actions and decisions matter, that they can run out of time, that they need to be strategic and quick. Ticking wristwatches seemed like a perfect match. I also wanted the audio to feel cinematic and visceral, so some type of exaggeration was also incorporated. 

Let’s listen to some examples of what came out of defining such aesthetic:


[url=https://soundcloud.com/user-369646377/sets/sound-of-world-war-i-field-hospital-part-1][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/e88c94c3ab2d4c8bdbd7c0ed6403260fef434fea.jpg[/img][/url]


Another question that presented itself along the way was: how to approach the top-down view. I’ve never worked with such a camera placement before, but I knew it would come with a unique set of technical challenges. 

After a few prototypes and discussions with our lead programmer Grzesiek, we decided to approach level audio as a set of vertical layers that will depend on the camera zoom. Luckily, thanks to our audio middleware Fmod, I could add such parameters to every sound I needed.

Here’s the film presenting how the “CameraDepth” parameter affects the sound emitters. Some layers are fading away, some are getting more reverb, and at some point, there’s only wind.


[previewyoutube=bJnBvNH9hBc;full][/previewyoutube]


That’s it for this Dev Diary. Hope you liked it!

notes.title: War Hospital Dev Diary#2: How We found the Right Atmosphere
notes.notes:
[b]Hi! Michał here, the art director for War Hospital. Today, I’d like to tell you about the process of looking for the visual atmosphere for our game, and the way we approached colors.[/b]

Disclaimer: I rarely start work without any research. Even when designing fantasy or sci-fi I like to find some references first. Usually, I’m not looking for anything specific. Instead, I’d rather go and search for something that would set the mood for my artwork. However, in the case of War Hospital, the process was slightly different. 

When you’re making a game where historical accuracy is crucial, the pre-designing process takes much more time than usual. Sometimes as much as half of the time you’re going to spend on the project! Especially when we’re talking about War Hospital.

I started by very precisely researching original documentaries and other useful information. 

It’s more than just photos and paintings of war scenes. These were necessary, but I also looked for interesting photos from the northern region of France. These were mostly contemporary photos of nature that gave me a fully colored view of the place, which wasn’t entirely accurate in colorized photos. I also used photos from the proper period to see the arrangement of villages, roads, and such). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/9c76d2d003d0d6f59bf3dd50fcb15f0b137e041d.jpg[/img]

Let’s say that I have to create a character based on our script. 

I have to determine how this particular type of unit will fit in our game and to do so, I need to know how its uniform looked, what equipment it should have, etc. Although our characters and their inventory are heavily stylized and exaggerated, their details need to match. Thus, I’m not starting painting until I have a strong, historical foundation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/e90af3e023e4ce9bcf184b4cdc5f9821be768ab7.jpg[/img]

I must say that creating the main characters, like Henry Wells or Sister Janet, was quite a challenge. 

Similarly looking at military uniforms doesn’t make the design any easier if you want to have unique and expressive characters. I dealt with it by shaking up smaller details of uniforms and equipment, and by differentiating body proportions, sometimes even to a point of caricature. There are also expressive, memorable faces that match the character description.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/16de50962283fd7ea0ed6b27e4d14d0739b71f13.jpg[/img]

In terms of environment the process is quite similar, but with small differences. 

The main buildings in our game are very different from typical military barracks and tents from World War I. 

They are like this because we want them to be as interesting as possible. Still, if you look closely, you will see some more traditionally militaristic elements such as tent sheathings, furniture, packs, or boxes. Combining the two, I’m able to develop buildings totally unique in form, but with an atmosphere suitable for a British WWI base.

One considerable challenge was creating the whole town where most of War Hospital gameplay takes place. As the main reference, I decided to use the French town of Rochefort-en-Terre, which remembers the medieval times. It became my basis for the general look of buildings. On the other hand, I used my architectural education to create the town layout. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/a345d579ff47fe3e79e62df9b1cdba18561c978d.jpg[/img]

Besides everything I’ve discussed above, I also created mood boards and atmospheric art. Here I have to thank our wonderful 3D artists that did a fantastic job putting my ideas into the game engine.

One of the most important goals for me was to avoid the greyish color palette typical for WWI and WWII games. 

We tend to identify the past with desaturated colors due to the way it was archived - via black-and-white or sepia photography. But the early 20th Century wasn’t monochromatic at all. With War Hospital, we got a chance to create a fresh and good-looking world, both diverse and colorful, that breaks with the tradition of war visuals. 

Adding color doesn’t take away from the tense atmosphere. On the contrary, it grounds it, making it much more relatable. We aren’t looking at some alien planet with a brown filter anymore. It’s our world, and this horrific conflict takes place in our backyard.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/8f946526815812520b7fe0d1154807d566c773f8.jpg[/img]

Did you like this inside look at game development? Wishlist and follow War Hospital, and join me next time in our Dev Diary!

notes.title: The Art of War | War Hospital Dev Diary #1
notes.notes:
Hi, I’m Michał Sztuka. From the very beginning, there were many ideas about how War Hospital should look. Many of them have changed or become abandoned, but the core remained unchanged. We wanted to show the cruel realities of The Great War as attractive to the player, but without losing historical reality.
 
[h2]Our goal was to make the art style recognizable among other war games. Their artistic convention is mostly grayish and dark because of the focus on historical accuracy.[/h2]

At the same time, there are war-themed games with a more attractive and epic look that 
makes them more like historical fantasy than anything.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/5d19eb4b97b84399ddc2ff296c988da51ed391c5.jpg[/img]

We wanted to find something in between, which made my work quite a challenge. I couldn’t just let my imagination run wild. 
 
To give War Hospital its own personality, we decided to base it on the historical accuracy of World War I, but make specific elements delicately stylized. They are still grounded in reality, yet slightly unreal, which makes them unique and interesting. For example, we changed body proportions a bit, or made small changes to the uniforms, equipment, or elements of the environment.

[h2]I won’t hide the fact that from the very beginning our main design inspirations were Dishonored and Dishonored 2. [/h2]

If you look at Dishonored characters, you can tell these are humans, but there is something special about them. We analyzed their designs, however with time, our ideas evolved. Still, if you see our early concept art, you’ll notice similarities. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/b4c0baea0a399ddab481cce171db7d56744a5ef5.jpg[/img]

One of the reasons we started looking for a different approach is the fact we’re not making a first-person game. In the case of War Hospital, a strategy, the key part is the environment. The players spend most of their game time looking at the main base from above, so we needed to make the whole place interesting. It was quite a challenge because of the real life setting, which indeed was dark, greyish and monotonous. Also, the military environment doesn’t really encourage experimentation, considering that every single building looks almost the same. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40165774/73dba3a41d4d7ee7f4d107bc51f2b47ef6037619.jpg[/img]

[h2]We decided to make our main buildings look makeshift; a mix of military assets and stuff found just laying around.[/h2]
 
This gave us lots of possibilities to make every military structure unique. We also decided to overscale most of the environment, such as city buildings, nature, and ground elements. We managed to get into this by adopting a specific way of sculpting objects such as stones, bricks, wooden parts etc. As a result, they are now much more expressive.

Another key element to enlivening the atmosphere was the way we illuminate the environment. Lighting gave us the opportunity to differentiate one place from another, even if structure-wise, they look similar. You will see that we show the reality of war in a very pleasant and surprisingly colorful way, yet without sacrificing the mood.

[h2]But how to add humanity to a war game you see from afar?[/h2]

This is a problem faced especially by strategy game designers. In RTS games like ours, a soldier is often reduced to a tiny blob that rushes at a target and dies. We wanted every unit to feel like a living person, so we created many additional visual assets, such as portraits or scene representations. These are our visual aids to emphasize the dramatism of situations that take place in your military hospital. They elevate these “grain of sand” units to the position of human beings whose life truly counts.

[b]Did you like this inside look at game development? Wishlist and follow War Hospital, and join me next time. We’ll talk closely about the various aspects of the color palette.[/b]

notes.title: Welcome to Command HQ!
notes.notes:
Hello, nice to have you here!

We’re Brave Lamb Studio, the team behind War Hospital. Thank you for your interest in our game! 

If you’re here, it means you won’t mind a unique take on war-themed games. That’s exactly what we aim to deliver.

We believe that World War I is such an underexplored setting. It’s fascinating--the first conflict of this scope in history--yet still unknown to many. As history buffs, we’ve always wanted to make a game about it. On the other hand, we didn’t want to create anything generic. 

“In war, medics are gods.” We don’t remember who said it, but it stuck with us. The idea of making War Hospital was born from these words.

We don’t recall many games about combat medics, especially ones that show the strategic/survival aspect of being a medical officer. Well, we want to change it! 

If you’d like to join us in this journey, please follow us, or add our game to your wishlist.  

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1553000/War_Hospital/][img]https://media.giphy.com/media/JyCVHEPGKKQxArnQvQ/giphy.gif[/img][/url]

Thanks, and see you in the next update!
